survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2022 Spain microdata (students nested in schools and autonomous communities) and reports a multilevel hierarchical linear model (MLwiN 2.36). The manuscript does not report the use of PISA sampling weights or any replicate-weight procedure, nor does it name any weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT). Because the analysis is a multilevel regression rather than a PV-based ML pipeline, the authors’ weighting strategy is not documented; therefore, the results should be interpreted as conditional on the analytic sample rather than explicitly population-representative estimates. The only explicit data-preparation step described is listwise deletion after confirming MCAR with Little’s test.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2022 Spain student sample aged 15–16 from 935 schools (966 educational centres initially). Excluded 2,008 students due to incomplete information across all variables. Missing values were assessed as MCAR using Little’s test (SPSS 29), and listwise deletion was applied (complete cases only), justified by the small proportion of deleted data (~6%) and the need to preserve the integrity of the composite socio-economic index.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 (Spain) Grade 15-16 Mathematics competence (Rasch scale; PVs averaged)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multilevel null model: Constant 479.98 (SE 5.19); variance components—Students 6160.93 (SE 49.66), Schools 1178.77 (SE 63.16), Autonomous community 610.37 (SE 202.48); Restricted log likelihood 353699.55; AIC 353715.55. Level-1 explanatory model: Constant 468.59 (SE 4.76); Gender −7.45 (SE 0.61); ISEC 13.52 (SE 0.49); Family cultural capital 6.28 (SE 0.47); Math anxiety −9.26 (SE 0.56); Self-efficacy in mathematics 7.64 (SE 0.33). Reported effect sizes: anxiety eta-squared η²=0.063 (medium); self-efficacy eta-squared η²=0.012 (small).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 (Spain) Grade 15–16 Mathematics competence the study leveraged Gender, Student socioeconomic context, Family cultural capital, Mathematics anxiety, and Self-efficacy in mathematics to model mathematics competence, finding that girls scored lower than boys (Gender −7.45) and that Mathematics anxiety had a negative association (−9.26) while Self-efficacy in mathematics had a positive association (7.64). This indicates that strengthening mathematics self-efficacy and reducing math anxiety—alongside addressing socioeconomic and cultural capital disparities—may improve students’ mathematics outcomes, though the study is observational and does not establish causal effects.

data.outcome_summary: This study analyzes PISA 2022 Spain student data (ages 15–16) using a three-level hierarchical model (students nested in schools and autonomous communities). The final analytic sample comprises 28,792 students from 935 schools, after excluding 2,008 students with incomplete information; missingness was assessed as MCAR and handled via listwise deletion. Mathematics competence is measured on the PISA mathematics scale (mean 500, SD 100) and the study uses ten plausible values, averaging them to obtain the dependent score. The multilevel results show that gender differences are statistically significant, mathematics anxiety is negatively associated with performance (η²=0.063, medium effect), and mathematics self-efficacy is positively associated (η²=0.012, small effect), alongside positive associations for socioeconomic context and family cultural capital. The manuscript does not report the use of PISA sampling/replicate weights, so population-representativeness and standard error calibration may be limited; additionally, the design is ex post facto, so causal claims cannot be inferred.
